new.tovw: Lead grade D: county history only; the addition is placed by the 1874 atlas, the house is not
new.n: Tim Bigelow's bogus-coin 'mint', Riverside, between Lyons and Camanche
new.pl: Riverside addition, north end of Clinton toward Lyons (1874 atlas); the log house and the lime-kiln are not placed
new.st: The 1879 History of Clinton County (p. 345) tells of Tim Bigelow's counterfeiting 'mint' in a log house at Riverside, below Davis's lime-kiln between Lyons and Camanche, warned by bell-wires run from the slough and Mill Creek bridges. The 1874 Clinton Co atlas, Clinton city plate shows 'Riverside' as the north-end addition of Clinton City on the river toward Lyons; the kiln and bridge are not legible. Pin is the Riverside addition, not the house.
new.t: Dies and bogus coin would be the relics, but Riverside is now city blocks: look only. A Clinton Sanborn or the 1886 county atlas may show the old lime-kiln.
src: History of Clinton County, Iowa (1879), p. 345

pinev: Approximate point for the Riverside addition read off the 1874 city plate (41.875, -90.18), on land about 800 m W of the Mississippi centreline (USA Rivers and Streams); no Clinton street or address layer could be checked from here, so the spot within the north end is not confirmed; r800.
